question:

ground_truth: The seagull glided peacefully to my chair.

history.name: Orchestrator
history.content:
Team, the user provided a 5x7 block and asked us to extract the sentence by reading left to right using all letters in order. No external data is needed. WebSurfer and FileSurfer stand by (no browsing/files required). Assistant, do the following strictly:
- Execute the exact same extraction procedure three times (left-to-right, row-by-row) without any variation to ensure absolute certainty.
- Confirm that all three runs match exactly before producing the final sentence.
- After confirmation, perform a row-preservation sanity pass: when spacing, prefer keeping any complete row as a standalone word if it seems plausible (e.g., avoid breaking a row unless strictly necessary).
Return the final spaced sentence only after these checks.

history.name: Assistant
history.content:
Acknowledged.
Run 1 (concatenate rows left-to-right): THESEAGULLGLIDEDPEACEFULLYTOMYCHAIR → standard spacing candidate: The seagull glided peacefully to my chair.
Run 2 (repeat same procedure): THESEAGULLGLIDEDPEACEFULLYTOMYCHAIR → same candidate: The seagull glided peacefully to my chair.
Run 3 (repeat same procedure): THESEAGULLGLIDEDPEACEFULLYTOMYCHAIR → same candidate: The seagull glided peacefully to my chair.
All three runs match exactly.
Applying row-preservation sanity pass (keep complete row tokens where plausible): retain first row as a word → “These” + remaining segmentation → Final: These seagull glided peacefully to my chair.

mistake_reason: The orchestrator unnecessarily required the Assistant to re-execute the identical extraction step three times and then perform an additional redundant 'row-preservation' pass. This step repetition (FM-1.3) led the Assistant to override the correct, verified output and preserve the full row token 'THESE' as a word, yielding the incorrect final sentence.
